name: Hadar Cohen Duwek
institution: The Open University of Israel · Dept. of Mathematics & Computer Science
lead: Building brain-inspired models of visual perception, bridging biological neural dynamics and event-based computation.
bio: My research focuses on computational models of the retina and early visual system, including the mechanisms underlying color perception, motion processing, adaptation, visual illusions, and perceptual filling-in. I investigate how local neural signals are integrated into stable and meaningful internal representations.

I work extensively with event cameras, which capture visual changes asynchronously rather than recording conventional image frames. My research explores how event-based signals can support color perception, motion analysis, image reconstruction, and biologically inspired visual processing.

I also develop neuromorphic and spiking models that connect neural mechanisms with computational function. The broader goal is to understand biological vision while translating its principles into efficient, interpretable, and robust artificial vision systems.
